_patient.input_block:
72F, EW EMER. admission from PHYSICIAN REFERRAL.
OUTCOME: discharged alive to SKILLED NURSING FACILITY
PRESENTING SYMPTOMS: Rash and other nonspecific skin eruption; Bacteriuria
PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS: Hypercalcemia
ACTIVE DIAGNOSES: Hypercalcemia; Secondary hyperparathyroidism of renal origin; Acute kidney failure, unspecified; Moderate protein-calorie malnutrition; Chronic kidney disease, stage 4 (severe); Pain due to genitourinary prosthetic devices, implants and grafts, initial encounter; Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease; Anemia in chronic kidney disease; Unspecified asthma, uncomplicated; Nonrheumatic aortic (valve) stenosis; Postprocedural hypothyroidism; Dehydration; Calcific tendinitis of right shoulder; Pruritus, unspecified; Pressure-induced deep tissue damage of other site; Adverse effect of other antacids and anti-gastric-secretion drugs, initial encounter; Adverse effect of vitamins, initial encounter
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Contact with and (suspected) exposure to COVID-19; Personal history of nicotine dependence; Long term (current) use of insulin; Body mass index [BMI] 28.0-28.9, adult; Encounter for attention to cystostomy; Do not resuscitate
PROCEDURES: Drainage of Bladder with Drainage Device, Percutaneous Approach; Change Drainage Device in Bladder, External Approach
MEDICATIONS: HYDROmorphone (Dilaudid) 2mg PO/NG; Polyethylene Glycol 17g PO/NG; Heparin 5000UNIT SC; Glucose Gel 15g PO; Ciprofloxacin HCl 250mg PO/NG; Levothyroxine Sodium 25mcg PO/NG; Sodium Bicarbonate 650mg PO/NG; Pantoprazole 20mg PO; Atorvastatin 10mg PO/NG; Miconazole Powder 2% 1Appl TP; Sarna Lotion 1Appl TP; Glucagon 1mg IM; Acetaminophen 650mg PO/NG; Insulin 0UNIT SC; Sodium Chloride 0.9% 1000mL IV; Lidocaine 5% Patch 1PTCH TD; FoLIC Acid 1mg PO/NG; amLODIPine 7.5mg PO/NG; Vial 1VIAL IV; CefTRIAXone 1gm IV; TraMADol 25mg PO; Sodium Chloride 0.9%  Flush 3-10mL IV; Fexofenadine 60mg PO; Dextrose 50% 12.5gm IV
MICROBIOLOGY: URINE: PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA [GENTAMICIN=S, TOBRAMYCIN=S, CEFTAZIDIME=R, CIPROFLOXACIN=S, PIPERACILLIN/TAZO=R, CEFEPIME=I, MEROPENEM=S]
SERVICES: MED
WARDS: Emergency Department; Surgery
_patient.note:
[1] The patient presented with rash and nonspecific skin eruption and bacteriuria.
[2] The primary diagnosis was hypercalcemia.
[3] Active diagnoses included hypercalcemia, secondary hyperparathyroidism of renal origin, acute kidney failure, unspecified, moderate protein-calorie malnutrition, chronic kidney disease, stage 4, pain due to genitourinary prosthetic devices, implants and grafts, initial encounter, type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease, anemia in chronic kidney disease, unspecified asthma, nonrheumatic aortic (valve) stenosis, postprocedural hypothyroidism, dehydration, calcific tendinitis of right shoulder, pruritus, unspecified, pressure-induced deep tissue damage of other site, adverse effect of other antacids and anti-gastric-secretion drugs, initial encounter, and adverse effect of vitamins, initial encounter.
[4] Past medical history included contact with and (suspected) exposure to COVID-19, personal history of nicotine dependence, long term (current) use of insulin, body mass index [BMI] 28.0-28.9, adult, encounter for attention to cystostomy, do not resuscitate.
[5] Procedures performed included drainage of bladder with drainage device, percutaneous approach, and change drainage device in bladder, external approach.
[6] Medications administered included HYDROmorphone, polyethylene glycol, heparin, glucose gel, ciprofloxacin HCl, levothyroxine sodium, sodium bicarbonate, pantoprazole, atorvastatin, miconazole powder, sarna lotion, glucagon, acetaminophen, insulin, sodium chloride, lidocaine patch, folic acid, amlodipine, vial, cefTRIAXone, tramadol, sodium chloride flush, fexofenadine, and dextrose 50%.
[7] Urine culture grew PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA, which was sensitive to GENTAMICIN, TOBRAMYCIN, CIPROFLOXACIN, PIPERACILLIN/TAZO, MEROPENEM, and resistant to CEFTAZIDIME and CEFEPIME.
[8] The patient was managed by the MED service.
[9] The patient was admitted to the Emergency Department and Surgery wards.
[10] The patient was discharged alive to a skilled nursing facility.
